episode_title: From 3 Sales to 500: What Actually Changed in Noemie Jouas' Launch Strategy

real_qa.q: What changed in Noemi Jouas' sewing pattern launch strategy between her first launch of three sales and her second launch of 500 patterns sold?
real_qa.r: Noemi shifted from replicating tactics used by others to posting authentic, already-recorded content without pressure for polish. She built momentum organically through engagement-focused videos and giveaways that grew her email list from 300 to 6,000 subscribers. She launched on a Friday instead of Monday, used a 30% discount code for 24 hours, and leveraged archival content from a failed product launch a year prior to build the narrative around the January skirt pattern.
real_qa.requete: Noemi Jouas sewing patterns launch strategy 500 sales

real_qa.q: How did Noemi Jouas accidentally discover her most effective launch tactic for the January skirt pattern?
real_qa.r: She made a mistake by posting a giveaway engagement video to her main Instagram feed instead of her trial reels at 11:30 PM Japan time. The post received around 50-100 comments of people wanting to participate. She then used ManyChat automation to have commenters type 'January' to receive a Flowdesk link where they could enter their emails, building a direct pipeline to send launch day discount codes to interested followers.
real_qa.requete: Noemi Jouas Instagram giveaway ManyChat Flowdesk launch tactic

real_qa.q: What specific advice did Jess, a pattern mentor, give Noemi Jouas about the timing of her sewing pattern launches?
real_qa.r: Jess advised Noemi to launch on a Friday instead of Monday because people search for sewing patterns over the weekend, similar to how music is released on Fridays. After implementing this change, Noemi noticed her patterns consistently see an uptick from Thursday through Sunday, confirming that hobbyist sewers are most active and interested in buying patterns around weekends.
real_qa.requete: why launch sewing patterns Friday instead Monday Noemi Jouas

real_qa.q: Why does having 55,000 social media followers not guarantee successful product sales for Noemi Jouas?
real_qa.r: An audience does not automatically translate to a business without the right launch strategy, email list growth, and understanding of customer needs. Noemi's first pattern launch with 55,000 followers yielded only three sales because she had not yet built a substantial email list (only 200-300 subscribers) or identified what her audience actually wanted to buy versus what she assumed they would purchase.
real_qa.requete: audience followers not equal business Noemi Jouas 55000

real_qa.q: What product naming mistake did Noemi Jouas identify in other aspiring pattern designers' launches?
real_qa.r: Designers were using generic style names like 'A-line skirt' as product names, making them unsearchable and indistinguishable from thousands of other similar items online. Noemi created unique product names—the June Top and January Skirt—so customers could specifically search for and find her patterns, building brand recognition and differentiation in the marketplace.
